html:
A series of wars fought mostly in the German lands of the Holy Roman Empire from 1618 to 1648. It began as a fight between Catholics and Protestants and grew into a European struggle for power. It was one of the most destructive wars in European history.

The spark came in Prague in 1618, when Protestant nobles of Bohemia threw two imperial officials out of a window and rebelled against the Catholic Habsburg emperor Ferdinand II. The emperor crushed them in 1620. Denmark entered and was beaten. Then in 1630 Sweden under King Gustavus Adolphus landed in Germany and won great victories, until he was killed at Lützen in 1632. In 1635 Catholic France joined the Protestant side, because it feared the Habsburgs more than it cared about religion.

Armies of mercenaries lived off the land, looting and burning. Hunger and plague followed them, made worse by the cold years of the Little Ice Age. Many German regions lost a third or more of their people.

The Peace of Westphalia in 1648 ended it. Each ruler kept the right to choose his state's religion, which settled the quarrel opened by the Reformation and hardened after the Council of Trent. Sweden and France gained land, the Dutch Republic and Swiss were recognised as independent, and Brandenburg grew. The emperor's power over the German princes was hollowed out.
